profiles.note: Architecture proposal; capacities are provisional. All ownership and rollback mechanisms remain present.

required_interfaces.handshake: ready/valid, no partial advancement across fetch context changes
all valid lanes in a group accept atomically, or none; no partial mutations
killed, recycled or stale tags cannot wake
Decoupled holds stable until ready; complete lifecycle validation before state update
contiguous oldest ready prefix of <=retire width; exception instruction never commits
no speculative visible write; non-idempotent reads and MMIO serialized
older preserved, younger invalidated, late responses rejected
ordered per-instruction record, including simultaneous two retire and exact fault boundary

invariants.rule: Every state key has exactly one mutable owner; consumers use explicit read-only projections or transactions.
Dispatch group allocation is atomic across ROB, IQ, RAT, PRF/free list and LSQ; no resources consumed on failure.
Every completion and wakeup validates full live lifetime identity; killed/late responses cannot mutate a new slot.
Only a contiguous oldest ready retirement prefix may commit; a faulting uop and all younger uops never commit.
Speculative stores, atomics and non-idempotent MMIO effects never externalize before precise commit permission.
Recovery preserves older ROB entries and reconstitutes speculative RAT/free-list mapping for precisely the survivors.
Dual dispatch handles within-group RAW/WAW and x0; dual retire handles older and younger trap/csr/fence conflicts.
An external transaction id outlives its ROB token if needed; cancel drains or discards the transport response safely.
PTW sees latest coherent PTE including dirty DCache state; SFENCE.VMA/FENCE.I enforce their respective visibility domains.
FP results/fflags/FS state update only on matching in-order commit; squashed FP operations have no CSR side effects.
AXI width/txn/CDC, PMA, device map and PHY state remain outside the CPU architectural backend.
Hardware bitstream and Debian LP64D claims require explicit board and software qualification, never inferred from virtual FPGA Linux.

g1_selected_decisions.decision: explicit integer PRF + speculative/committed RAT + bitset FreeList + per-destination reverse undo log
g1_selected_decisions.reset: x0 fixed to physical 0; integer architectural x1..x31 map to phys1..31; FreeList contains physical 32..N-1; x0 never allocates, releases, or writes
g1_selected_decisions.allocation: rename lane order: read sources from speculative RAT including prior accepted lane writes, reserve free physical destination, retain old mapping in ROB undo entry, then set speculative RAT; grant is atomic with ROB/IQ/LSQ permits
g1_selected_decisions.commit: update committed RAT on normal in-order retirement, free stale destination once when its replacing instruction commits; no free when completion merely arrives; no free on instruction that does not write
g1_selected_decisions.recovery: on validated non-head branch mispredict, stop rename and architectural retire; squash only instructions younger than surviving branch by ROB age; walk their rename undo entries in reverse order (youngest first), restore each old mapping in speculative RAT and free only their newly allocated destinations; keep older in-flight and branch; for synchronous trap, retire any permitted older prefix then unwind all uncommitted entries to committed RAT
g1_selected_decisions.completion: check live RobToken and producer/value allocation generation before PRF write or IQ wakeup; no stale writes after squash/reallocate; async memory transaction lifetime separate
g1_selected_decisions.future: G2 two-lane rename adds intra-group bypass and 2 physical destination allocators; branch snapshots optional optimization, not a G1 correctness requirement; do not change RecoveryCut interface when optimizing
g1_selected_decisions.rationale: Small FPGA G1 can tolerate multi-cycle recovery and fewer read/write ports. Checkpointing all speculative mappings and free-list state per branch adds state/collision complexity and may be justified later by measured PPA/IPC, not assumed.
g1_selected_decisions.nax_alternative: NaxRiscv commit-reschedule dual speculative/committed RAT with dirty-bit selector; may replace per-younger undo strategy only if same identity/precise recovery contracts and FPGA PPA pass; no simultaneous duplicate state owner

g1_selected_decisions.decision: new one-source product core namespace, stable semantic/platform seams extracted once; retain Tiny v2 as independent qualified regression/golden reference
g1_selected_decisions.boundary: ProductCore must not instantiate or inherit TinyRob, TinyDependencyBackend, TinyMemoryBackend, TinyLoadQueueMemoryBackend or TinyPagedCore. A temporary named semantic adapter may consume TinySemanticDecode only until its shared owner extraction, but no product backend state may come from v2.
g1_selected_decisions.first_code_change: extract DecodedInstruction/semantic decode ownership exactly once with a v2 compatibility adapter, not a parallel copied C decoder; keep existing CoreConfig.capability check intact so F/D is not falsely advertised
g1_selected_decisions.software_and_soc: keep AetherSoC v0 boot/AXI/UART/PLIC/ACLINT platform frozen; add a separately selectable ProductCoreComplex/SoC adapter only after minimal core retirement test passes, never silently replace the v0 build
g1_selected_decisions.target_config: new ProductCoreConfig initially IMA(M/S/U, Sv39) with F/D false until implemented. Preserve ISA vs ABI separation and verify new LP64D profile only at G3.
g1_selected_decisions.no_legacy_mutation: G1 product PR must not modify v2 Tiny ROB/rename/LSU in order to make product backend compile; any shared semantic extraction must run the v2 regression suite.

g1_release_gates.contract_review: The D02/D06 approach is selected and must be reviewed before a production RTL branch. D01/D03/D04/D05 remain unresolved; no claim of completed G0 freeze until maintainers accept architecture and proof obligations.
g1_release_gates.initial_geometry_rule: For no destination-pressure stalls at full ROB occupancy, integer PRF must have at least 32 + ROB entries. Smaller PRFs are legal but must encode dispatch backpressure; proposed 8/48, 16/64, 64/96 avoid this unnecessary first-order limit.
g1_release_gates.changelog: G3 candidate integer PRF raised from 64 to 96 because ROB64 with only 32 spare integer physical registers could not accommodate 64 simultaneous destination-producing inflight uOps.

naxriscv_reference.recovery_tradeoff: G1 reverse undo is a proposed proof/reference strategy, not a permanent FPGA requirement; benchmark Nax-style speculative/committed dual RAT + dirty-mask rollback without changing RecoveryCut contract
naxriscv_reference.physical_int_observation: Nax Gen.scala uses an example ROB64 with integer physicalDepth64; our PRF96 is a throughput-capacity candidate, not correctness minimum. Allow backpressure and measure FPGA PPA.
